Hi there, As per rule, the policy will get lapsed in case you don't pay the premiums even during the grace period ( i.e, 15 days post the payment date in case of monthly/quarterly/semi annually and 30 days in case of annually)
You can renew the policy if you want but that would be subject to a medical checkup if needed and you will have to pay interest/penalty charges as well.

comments.text:
Limited pay may help some premium payers to give piece of mind that I am done with my payments and I don't need to do it for some many years and forget to pay some premiums down the line. 

However, this option is most beneficial for Insurance companies. They will get their premiums upfront and the below are the advantages:

1. In case of life risk early into your payment schedules, the company would be better off as they got the money realized already. They can generate return on your premium paid to recover the paid sum assured in the coming years.

2. As they explained in the video, instead paying a bigger sum upfront, you keep paying the smaller amount until tenure ends. As times goes by value of money goes down. The amount you are not paying as premium can generate returns with good compounding. So, company want to take away this compounding advantage from the customer to themselves.
